candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication adverse effects, client education, safe administration and evaluation of medication response
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — glimepiride / sulfonylurea hypoglycemia safety
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients starting glimepiride that severe hypoglycemia is a clinically important risk and that they need to recognize/manage low glucose and follow prescribed meal and medication instructions.

options.A: Glimepiride can cause severe hypoglycemia, so learn how to recognize and manage low glucose and follow meal/medication instructions
options.B: Glimepiride cannot cause clinically important hypoglycemia when taken without insulin
options.C: Glimepiride is intended to treat type 1 diabetes and diabetic ketoacidosis
options.D: Glimepiride should routinely be taken during prolonged fasting because missing calories reduces adverse effects

candidate.rationale: The current glimepiride prescribing information warns that all sulfonylureas, including glimepiride, can cause severe hypoglycemia and states that patients must be educated to recognize and manage it. Hypoglycemia is more likely when caloric intake is deficient and in several vulnerable populations. Glimepiride is indicated for adults with type 2 diabetes and is not effective for type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Glimepiride can cause severe hypoglycemia and requires patient education on recognition/management; it is a type 2 diabetes drug and should be taken according to meal-linked instructions.
candidate.source_locator: §5.1 Hypoglycemia: all sulfonylureas including glimepiride can cause severe hypoglycemia; patients must be educated to recognize/manage hypoglycemia; risk increases with deficient caloric intake and specified vulnerable conditions. §1 Indications/Limitations: type 2 diabetes; not for type 1 diabetes or DKA. §2.1: administer with breakfast or first main meal
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
candidate.stem: A client with type 2 diabetes is starting glimepiride. Which safety teaching is most important for the nurse to include?
